title: 1981 AHSME Problem 21
statement: In a triangle with sides of lengths \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c,\) \[ (a+b+c)(a+b-c)=3ab. \] The measure of the angle opposite the side of length \(c\) is

solutions.text:
The condition gives \((a+b)^2-c^2=3ab,\) so \[ c^2=a^2+b^2-ab. \] If \(\theta\) is opposite \(c,\) the law of cosines says \(c^2=a^2+b^2-2ab\cos\theta.\) Therefore \(2ab\cos\theta=ab,\) so \(\cos\theta=\frac{1}{2}\) and \(\theta=60^\circ.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is D.
hints: Expand the left side as a difference of squares
Compare the resulting expression for \(c^2\) with the law of cosines
